body:
Hey,

mini.ai ships many textobjects, including a tag one, which can be used with `t`. However, the default object does not cover _every_ edge case. For the longest time, I've been using a custom object, taken from [Lazyvim](https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/42c9f7152b9bd1a4f739b115390370c208dc2a55/lua/lazyvim/plugins/coding.lua#L51). But it also misses some even crazier edge cases.

Today I was investigating this situation and realized that a better solution can be achieved with [nvim-treesitter-textobjects](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects). It just so happens that tags (`elements`) are "tagged" [as functions](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects/blob/master/queries/html/textobjects.scm). Which means that if you're using 

```lua
f = ai.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = "@function.outer", i = "@function.inner" }),
```

It will also work flawlessly with tags! Still getting used to it, but it's a creative "workaround" that I felt I had to share!

comment_data.bodyHTML:
Thanks for sharing!

This is more or less recommended way to handle more complex tags. But instead of globally overriding f, the suggested approach is to:

  • Create filetype plugin(s) for filetype(s) you want to have "enhanced" tree-sitter based tag textobject. For example, '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/html.lua'.

  • Set buffer-local config that sets t textobject to use gen_spec.treesitter. So something like this:

    if _G.MiniAi ~= nil then
  vim.b.miniai_config = {
    custom_textobjects = {
      t = MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = '@function.outer', i = '@function.inner' }),
    },
  }
end

title: [mini.ai] Functions as an alternative text-object for tags
